web.title: Can Large Language Models forecast carbon price movements? Evidence from Chinese carbon markets
web.description: * •We propose an effective two-stage forecasting framework for carbon markets, combining a Time-Series model with Large Language Models. * •The Chain-of-Thought methodology enables the LLM to improve Time-Series model predictions by reflecting on past deviations from actual market prices. * •Incorporating sentiment labels derived from market news enhances the LLM’s ability to capture market dynamics and improves the accuracy of carbon price forecasts. ... This paper investigates the impact of Large Language Models (LLMs) on forecasting Chinese carbon prices. We introduce a novel two-stage forecasting framework integrating a Time-Series Model (TSM) and Large Language Models. Initially, we use historical data on Chinese Emission Allowance prices to train the TSM for preliminary predictions. LLMs then refine these predictions, which process a sequence of past and corresponding future prices as a chain of thought. Additionally, we utilize the LLM to analyze and categorize the sentiment of news headlines, generating market sentiment labels that enhance the LLM’s predictive accuracy. Our findings indicate that LLMs can improve TSM forecasts by 28–38 % across different regional markets. Furthermore, incorporating news sentiment labels into the LLM contributes an additional reduction in forecasting deviations, ranging from 3–4 %. ... from the lack of sufficient data in novel markets, as well as the presence of non-linearity and volatility, rendering traditional prediction methods less effective. To tackle this challenge, we propose enhancing carbon price forecasting by integrating machine-learning-based Time-Series Models with recent advancements in ... In recent years, the progress of Artificial Intelligence (AI) such as Machine Learning has sparked emerging research into their impact on financial research, including market trend prediction (Gu et al., 2020), energy price forecasting (Chai et al., 2023), financial textual analysis (Loughran and McDonald, 2016), and corporate governance (Gofman and Jin, 2024). Especially, the recent emerging Large Language Models (LLMs) have been proven to possess robust knowledge-learning capability (Brown et al., 2020, Ouyang et al., 2022). Through pre-training on extensive human knowledge, LLMs acquire a rich understanding not only of human languages but also of mathematical deduction and reasoning (Wei et al., 2022), as well as financial marketing (Sun et al., 2021, Zhou and Wang, 2021, Li and Liu, 2023). In our study, we employ LLMs to improve the accuracy of the Time-Series Model estimates and to analyze financial sentiment in news headlines related to carbon emissions. We aim to address the following critical research questions: Can LLMs comprehend the price trends within the Chinese carbon emission market? Do LLMs possess the capability to enhance the prediction outcomes of conventional machine learning models? Can LLMs effectively leverage sentiment signals from news headlines to forecast prices? To answer these questions, we develop a two-stage time-series forecasting framework integrating both a Time-Series Model and a Large Language Model. ... Thus, we propose to use LLMs to predict carbon price trends based on the past prediction results of the Autoformer models, that is, employing LLMs to refine the Autoformer’s prediction results. This refinement is achieved by providing the LLM with exemplary pairs of TSM’s raw predictions and actual future price sequences, prompting it to learn from past prediction deviations. This approach is supported by the following reasons. Firstly, Autoformer predictions have already incorporated market context for LLMs reference and are expected to help LLMs to better understand the carbon market trend. Secondly, Autoformer predictions suffer from past deviations as all Time-Series Models, while LLMs possess the ability to continuously learn from new data through fine-tuning, enabling them to adapt to evolving past price trends and enhance their prediction accuracy over time. Such advanced LLM prompting techniques are called Chain-of-Thought (CoT) and Self-Refine in the Artificial Intelligence area. The CoT technique enables successful predictions based on observable historical patterns, such as preceding periods, thereby providing the LLM with relevant market context. The Self-Refine procedure further encourages the LLM to actively reflect on past TSM predictive inaccuracies and refine its current predictions accordingly. Inspired by this, we propose to first utilize CoT to incorporate market context into future predictions provided by the LLM, followed by further prompting the LLM to refine its predictions based on reflection from past deviations. Therefore, our two-stage framework, incorporating the Time-Series Model and Large Language Models, enables the LLMs to account for market-context variations and yield forecast results more accurately than Autoformer models and direct prompt processes. Furthermore, after adding noise to the TSM prediction results inputted into the LLM, we find that only more accurate TSM results enable the LLM to make more accurate predictions. This indicates that the LLM is indeed capable of identifying carbon market price trends and further learning and refining from the TSM predictions. Next, we assess the LLM's capability for textual sentiment analysis by creating a sentiment label dataset of news headlines related to Chinese climate policy and carbon emissions events sourced from major news media. For each headline, we use LLM to assess whether it is positive, negative, or neutral for future carbon prices. We convert these responses into numerical scores and integrate them into LLM prediction. Additionally, we investigate whether incorporating such market sentiment data can enhance LLM’s ability to forecast carbon market price trends. Overall, we conducted a comprehensive series of empirical analyses to show that our CoT-RF methodology reduce the prediction MSE by 28–38 %, by reflecting on deviations of TSM predictions over preceding time steps. Moreover, by utilizing news sentiment labels as additional information provided to the LLM, we observe another 3–4 % improvement in our LLM-based methods. Our results show that increased model complexity improves not only information processing but also market context and sentiment comprehension. This suggests that utilizing an advanced TSM-LLMs time-series framework has the potential to significantly improve forecast accuracy. The observed pattern of CEA price predictability based on recent public news sentiment supports theories of delayed information diffusion and limited investor attention (Kahneman, 1973). ... We propose a novel two-stage framework that combines a state-of-the-art Time-Series model for initial predictions with LLMs to enhance and refine the forecasts. A key feature of our approach is the implementation of a self-reflection mechanism, enabling the LLM to learn from previous forecasting errors, thereby improving future predictions. ...
